title: Data Availability
description: The closed vocabularies describing how a metric's underlying data can be obtained (#870).
$comment: A wrapper object whose only job is to keep every $def reachable from the root: generate-types.ts runs json-schema-to-typescript with unreachableDefinitions:false, so a $def nothing points at emits no type. Same pattern as technology.v1.json and metric.v1.json. Callers $ref the individual $defs, not this object.

geographyCoverage.description: How geographically granular the underlying data is.
geographyCoverage.$comment: A coverage class, NOT a scope. It says the data resolves to individual countries; it does not say which. The entry's sibling 'geography' carries the scope.

timeResolution.description: How finely the underlying data is resolved over time.

dataFormat.description: Where the data can be obtained, and in what form.
dataFormat.$comment: #870 specifies this as one enum with parenthetical free|paywall ('tabular-in-pub (free|paywall)'). Split into dataFormat and access because the acceptance criteria call for the tables/text indicator and the free/paywall indicator as separate UI signals; a flat five-member enum would make the table string-match to recover them. 'In tool' means we host it -- those rows link to the timeseries download via the generated index. A downloadable non-timeseries value is expected here once the hosting mechanism is decided.

access.description: Whether reaching the data at the publisher costs money. Null when we host it.
access.$comment: Null exactly when dataFormat is 'In tool' -- a paywall on data we serve ourselves is a contradiction. draft-07 cannot tie two sibling properties together, so validateScopedEntries enforces the biconditional.
